clue.text: Credit card company with stock to purchase, including wine

indicators.note: the company's letters take in the wine, holding it within them

parts.note: a PLC is a public limited company, whose shares anyone may buy
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Describes a card firm that has shares on the market and also sells wine.
explanation.walkthrough: PLC stands for public limited company, a British firm whose shares are traded publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is informal for credit cards, from the material they are made of.

clue.text: Interrogates politician involved in matter

indicators.note: the politician is involved within the matter, placed inside it

parts.note: pus is matter from an infected wound
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone questions a politician mixed up in some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like an affair or issue; it is the yellowish fluid of an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information.

clue.text: Skill to take in short game that's extremely cunning

indicators.note: taking in means holding something within, so the shortened game goes inside

parts.note: art can mean skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: short means cut, so the game loses its last letter

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Skill is needed to master a brief game requiring great cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' is not an extremes signal here: extremely cunning is the superlative of arch, meaning sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means cunning or roguish, and archest is its superlative, the most sly.

clue.text: Smart pass is needed to enter banks from today

indicators.note: the pass letters enter, going inside the banks
the banks of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: an ID card serves as a pass

explanation.surface: From today, a smart pass is required to enter the banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks of today are T and Y, and ID enters between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and smart are synonyms for neat and well-ordered in appearance.

clue.text: Remarkable comic performing feature during TV show

indicators.note: performing letters act out a new routine, in a rearranged order

explanation.surface: A remarkable comedian's performance is the highlight of a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: On commercial television, advertisement interruptions recur in the middle of a programme.

clue.text: Hopper's earliest form? Piece in American bar

parts.note: a tad is a small amount, an American colloquialism
a pole is a long bar

explanation.surface: Asks about the first shape of some hopper, then mentions a piece in an American bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopper' looks like a person or an artist (Edward Hopper), but it is a frog, which begins life as a tadpole.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog hops, and its earliest stage of life is the tadpole, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Ace PM, Liz Truss, fighting with EU member might be lifted by this?

definitions.text: member might be lifted by this?

indicators.note: letters fighting are in disarray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praises PM Liz Truss as an ace fighting with the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like an EU member state; it is an arm, a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapezius in the upper back and shoulders helps raise the arm, a limb or member.

clue.text: Clone broken phone?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exact double of someone
second meaning, playful: a phone that no longer works is a ringer that is dead

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey literal reading of a phrase meaning a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is someone who looks exactly like another person, an identical double.

clue.text: Views hole: golf club's not right to tackle flag

indicators.note: tackle here means come up against, the club meeting the flag after it

parts.note: O is a hole, from its shape
the pin is the flagstick on a golf green

indicators.note: without the right letter, abbreviated R, which is removed

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer at a hole finds the club unsuitable for tackling the flag.
explanation.walkthrough: IRON without R gives ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief someone holds, so the singular matches one of these views.

clue.text: Jacks drunk Guinness when out of uniform

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering about in disorder
out of means without, so the uniform letter is removed from the pool

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Sailors drink Guinness when they are off duty and out of uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacks' looks like sailors (jack tars); a jack is also a flag flown at a ship's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a small national flag flown at sea, and ensigns are flags in the same sense.

clue.text: Tailless parrot and one cuckoo returning with a nut

indicators.note: without a tail, so the parrot's final letter is dropped

parts.note: a macaw is a large parrot

indicators.note: going back, so the letters for one and cuckoo are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
cuckoo means crazy, or mad

explanation.surface: A bird without its tail and a crazy one turn back holding a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: MACAW loses its last letter to give MACA; I plus MAD reversed gives DAMI; then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an Australian tree whose round edible kernel is a popular nut.

clue.text: Boxer considering that nickname

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer
as can mean since or because, i.e. considering that

explanation.surface: Talks about a boxer's nickname, given some consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed or alternative name, close to a nickname.

clue.text: Bring up latest information with centre for news

parts.note: the SP (starting price) is slang for the latest information or gen

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the inner pair of news

explanation.surface: Suggests raising the latest information at the centre for news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' looks like raising a topic; it means vomit. The SP is British slang for the inside story, from the starting price in horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up food is to vomit, which is what spew means.

clue.text: Going through here travelling: breakdown having missed parking sign

indicators.note: letters on the move are rearranged
missing something means leaving it out, so the parking letter is dropped

parts.note: parsing is the grammatical breakdown of a sentence
P is the road sign for parking

explanation.surface: Someone driving here suffers a breakdown and misses the parking sign.
explanation.walkthrough: HERE rearranged gives REHE; PARSING without its P gives ARSING. 'Breakdown' looks like a car failing; it is the analysis of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through a play or speech is to rehearse it, practising it before performance.

clue.text: Balances more than one pound; needs nerve at the start

indicators.note: puts the nerve letters at the beginning

parts.note: steel means resolve or nerve
a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a yard, so yards are several pounds

explanation.surface: Weighing more than a pound takes nerve at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the weight unit, fitting balances; it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is an old weighing device with a sliding weight on an arm, a kind of scales.

clue.text: Still crackling on vinyl record

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the noise or interference heard on a record

explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings of one word: an adjective for stillness and a noun for crackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Static describes something unmoving, and is also the electrical crackle of interference on audio.

clue.text: Time on strike proceeds with week out

indicators.note: the week's letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: winnings are the proceeds of gambling

explanation.surface: Suggests strike action and lost pay, a week out of proceeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' suggests industrial action; in cricket the batter on strike is the one facing the bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an innings is a team's or player's period of batting, its turn at the crease.

clue.text: Place for holiday transfer, ultimately — livid here, say, having lost all cases?

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so take the last letter of transfer
each word loses its outer letters, its case, keeping only its insides

explanation.surface: A holiday transfer goes wrong and a furious traveller has lost all their suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: R, then the insides of livid, here and say: IVI, ER, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera, the Mediterranean coast of France and Italy, is a famous holiday resort area.

clue.text: Turned down rubbish date

parts.note: refuse is rubbish or waste

explanation.surface: Someone was rejected for a date that went badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Refused means declined or rejected, which is what turned down means.

clue.text: Plain holiday home providing accommodation for one

indicators.note: the villa houses the other letters inside it

parts.note: a villa is a rented holiday house
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A modest holiday villa sleeping just one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is slang for ordinary or basic, without extras, from the plain ice cream flavour.

clue.text: Upset cricketer with small, silly thing?

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a sill is a ledge, so a sill-y thing is a ledge; the question mark flags the pun

explanation.surface: Some cricketer gets upset over a small, silly thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is also a cricket fielding position, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, to sledge is to unsettle a batter with taunts and verbal abuse.

clue.text: End of teaching assessment is harsh

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a rating is an assessment or grade

explanation.surface: A final assessment of teaching turns out harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating voice or sound is rough and jarring, unpleasantly abrasive.

clue.text: Waste time with lover — buoyant when excited …

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something

indicators.note: letters stirred up and excited are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles with a lover, buoyant when excited.
explanation.walkthrough: BUOYANT rearranged gives NYABOUT. The ellipsis links to the next clue's loving male.
explanation.definitionFit: To fanny about is British slang for to dither, messing around without doing anything useful.

clue.text: … loving male, naked in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: raw can mean bare or naked

explanation.surface: Continues the lover: an affectionate man, naked, in retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm describes affectionate, friendly feelings, so it fits loving as an adjective.

clue.text: Money put away: daughter to get married

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3 money supply
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: Money is saved up so a daughter can get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' looks like saving money; it means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mated means paired or coupled, as a pair joined in marriage.

clue.text: Do up home after power cut

indicators.note: a cut means removal, so the power letter is taken out

parts.note: someone's place is their home
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Fixing up a home after a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do up' looks like decorating; it means fastening shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace shoes is to fasten them by tying the strings.

clue.text: Very large pair regularly exposed in the Sun

parts.note: so can mean very, as in so good
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: only every other letter of pair is shown, giving its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A very large pair are exposed in the Sun, a tabloid picture of topless sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun' looks like the British tabloid newspaper; it is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to or found in the sun, the star at the centre of our system.

clue.text: Wine is used in this sauté with rich cooking

indicators.note: cooking up letters means mixing them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recipe: wine goes into a rich sauté as it cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface hides a church service: communion wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian sacrament in which consecrated bread and wine are shared.

clue.text: Order and ask about hot curry

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the hot letter
putting letters in a new order rearranges them

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A diner orders and asks about a hot curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like placing a restaurant order; it signals that the letters are rearranged before going round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhansak is a Parsi dish of meat cooked with lentils, served in curry houses.

clue.text: English team up before Germany came out

indicators.note: before places the team-up letters ahead of the Germany letter

parts.note: to merge is to combine or team up
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An English team-up before facing Germany emerged, like a football rivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, appearing from somewhere hidden.
